PILOT BRIEFING

Fly. Dodge. Upgrade.

Fly north (heading 000°) to increase your distance. Birds, air traffic, buildings, terrain, and power lines are solid hazards. A close pass earns a bonus after you clear the entire encounter.

Lower throttle with Left Alt to save fuel. Continue below idle to apply up to 40% reverse thrust and slow the aircraft; Shift brings the throttle forward again. The throttle slider and gamepad triggers also reach reverse. An empty tank cuts the engine; keep your airspeed up and glide toward a runway or clear, flat ground. Lower your gear, extend flaps, and touch down gently to finish the run. Fly below 80 meters above ground to build a low-flying bonus: the closer to the surface, the faster it grows, up to $20 per second. A safe landing after 500 meters adds $750 and doubles your distance, close-pass and low-flying earnings. Crashes scatter every aircraft part and shatter the struck obstacle. Ground impacts excavate craters and tear through paving; the camera follows the wreckage before results appear.

Every workshop level replaces a visible assembly. All purchased levels remain selectable in the workshop: click Stock or a Mk level, inspect it in 3D, then equip it for free. Select any upgrade or black-market module for a live, rotatable 3D inspection before buying. Each aircraft has seven exclusive futuristic modules; owned modules can be removed and reinstalled for free. Meridian, Peregrine and Astra black-market builds can break Mach 1, triggering a vapor cone and sonic boom (enable Sound). Each craft has a rated speed envelope: stock → all Mk V → full black market. Engine, wing and airframe upgrades raise that rating; fuel, efficiency and controls improve endurance and handling. Black-market parts replace the statistics of the workshop part in their slot. The fully upgraded Astra is capped at Mach 5, including in dives and at altitude. Damage to scenery, traffic and ground persists between runs and on this device. Your aircraft is always repaired and reloaded automatically for each run. Use Repair environment in the hangar or results to restore terrain and environment objects without changing your progress. Runway surfaces automatically repair when a new run starts.

Buy a unique missile system for any aircraft in the black market: Firefly, Comet, Nightjar or Nova. T selects or cycles visible moving targets ahead, then clears the lock after the last target; keep it in sight until the reticle turns green, then press X to fire a guided missile. X without a completed lock fires straight along the aircraft nose. Touch buttons provide the same controls. Aircraft hits earn $300, birds $90, environment objects $100, power cables $150, and new terrain strikes $35. Earnings are banked at the end of the run. Missiles have limited ammunition and reload every run. Cyan reload beacons spawn randomly ahead while you carry a missile system. Fly through the luminous ring to refill your entire magazine; a full magazine leaves the pack available. Locked targets must remain in sight; terrain and buildings block lock acquisition.

Jet and UFO maximum ratings use boost. Thrust, altitude, drag, gear and maneuvering affect the speed you can reach. Shop previews compare the installed and selected loadouts.

Animation runs on every display refresh with adaptive resolution targeting 60 FPS or higher. High-RPM props use shutter blur to prevent strobing; low-RPM blades and shop inspection remain fully detailed. The FPS counter shows the actual rate, which depends on your display and hardware.

Gamepad: left stick flies and clicking it toggles gear; right stick looks and clicking it cycles flaps; triggers adjust throttle, shoulders steer the rudder. A boosts; B brakes. On a runway, pull back above 55 knots in the Kestrel, 80 in the Meridian or 115 in the Peregrine. The stock Astra uses powered gravitic lift at low speeds; fuel exhaustion disables it. Climbing spends airspeed unless thrust overcomes gravity and drag. Descending trades altitude for speed, up to the drag-limited terminal speed.
